question: A patient with seasonal allergic rhinitis is started on an H1 antihistamine. Which of the following effects is NOT primarily mediated by H1 receptor stimulation?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Nasal itching IS mediated by H1 receptors on sensory nerve endings in the nasal mucosa. H1 antihistamines effectively relieve this symptom in allergic rhinitis.
Sneezing IS an H1-receptor-mediated reflex triggered by histamine stimulation of sensory nerve endings in the nasal mucosa.

Correct. Gastric acid secretion is mediated by H2 receptors on parietal cells, not H1 receptors. This is why H2 blockers (ranitidine, famotidine) are used for peptic ulcers, while H1 antihistamines treat allergic symptoms.
Rhinorrhoea in allergic rhinitis IS caused by H1-receptor-mediated increase in vascular permeability of nasal mucosal vessels, leading to plasma exudation.

overallFeedback.feedback: H1 receptors mediate allergic symptoms (itching, sneezing, rhinorrhoea, bronchoconstriction), while H2 receptors on parietal cells regulate gastric acid secretion — different receptors, different drug classes.
Excellent. Gastric acid secretion is an H2-receptor function — a key pharmacological distinction that determines which antihistamine class to use for which clinical indication.
